How it works

Three steps. No big-bang project.

Every engagement follows the same simple path: find where AI pays, prove it with something running, then take it to the next leader.

1

Find the ROI

We sit with your leaders and the people who do the work, map the business processes, and rank them by what automating each one would return.

  • Processes mapped with the people who run them
  • Ranked by return and feasibility
  • A shortlist, not a wish list
Where everyone starts2

Prove it with a demo pilot

We take the best process on the list and automate it with Claude Code — a working demo on your real workflow, so the ROI is something you can see, not a slide.

  • One process, built and running
  • The ROI case beside it
  • A clear yes / no on going further
3

Roll it out, leader by leader

Then we keep going. We work with each of your leaders in turn, moving their department to AI — one at a time, or across the company at once.

  • Each leader gets their own shortlist
  • Each department proven, then scaled
  • One platform tracking all of it

See how a rollout runs, department by department

The book behind the method

Trust before intelligence.

Why 95% of AI pilots fail. How 5% succeed.

Ram Katamaraja’s argument is the reason we work the way we do: an organization comes to trust its AI the same way it comes to trust its people — by seeing what they have actually shipped. That is why we start with a demo pilot you can see running, and why we move one leader at a time instead of announcing a transformation.

In practiceProve one process before scaling to ten.
In practiceWork inside the systems you already run.
In practiceMeasure readiness by what shipped, not who attended.
RK
Ram KatamarajaCEO, Colaberry · author of Trust Before Intelligence

Questions

Common questions.

Can we combine services?

Yes. For example, Build for a custom application while your people go through Train or Guide to automate the workflows around it.

Is Build an off-the-shelf product?

No. It is custom made and custom designed with your business experts, around how your company and your industry actually work.

Will Guide add another tool to our stack?

No. Your team builds workflows that run locally in your own environment and work with the systems you already have — your ERP, CRM, email, drives and chat.

Questions

About the numbers.

Why are there no prices on this page?

Build and Guide are scoped to your business, so a number before we have seen your processes would be a guess. Bring the two figures above and the conversation gets specific fast.

What does the Build down payment cover?

[Confirm] The start of the engagement — working with your experts, finding the ROI and the demo pilot. The monthly fee covers the ongoing design and build.

Why is Guide a 12-month engagement?

Training takes the first months; the rest is guided building across departments. A year is long enough for workflows to ship and for the capability to stay.

Is Train really $0 to start?

Yes. Open an account and your people can start. An FDE is assigned to manage your account.

The book behind the method

Trust before intelligence.

Why 95% of AI pilots fail. How 5% succeed.

Ram Katamaraja’s argument is the reason we work the way we do: an organization comes to trust its AI the same way it comes to trust its people — by seeing what they have actually shipped. From the page to the work

Three ideas from the book that shape every engagement.

01

Prove one before you scale ten.

Pilots fail when they are announced as transformations. Trust comes from seeing one thing work.

So weStart every Build and Guide engagement with a demo pilot on one real process.
02

Work where the work already lives.

AI that sits beside the business, in a separate tool, rarely becomes how the business runs.

So weBuild workflows inside your current systems, and applications designed around how you work.
03

Measure what shipped, not who attended.

Capability that cannot be evidenced is not capability.

So weCompute readiness from what your people build, not from course completion.
